coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: P11
names: P11 -- landscaped median strip connecting Mission Bay Circle to P11A
record.summary: A tree-lined median strip running within the road right-of-way, connecting the 'Mission Bay Circle' roundabout east to the P11A half-circle island; per this repository's own satellite trace (no outside source describes the strip), an already-landscaped median, hand-traced with the property owner's guidance and fit to a rotated rectangle. OCII's own September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P11/11A' together among the parcels SF Recreation and Parks will manage (not among the 'when built' parcels), consistent with it being complete by that date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- owner-guided satellite trace, idealized to a fitted rectangle rather than left as a raw hand-traced outline. Not a surveyed footprint or GIS file from the project team. street_clip_exempt=true: this is a real median strip that sits entirely within the paved road right-of-way by design -- clipping it against the generic street buffer would zero it out entirely, not correct a mispositioning. Owner-approved exception.
notes.digitized_from: Hand-traced from satellite imagery, guided directly by the owner's own marked-up screenshot (their drawn outline extracted from the photo via ORB feature-matching/homography), then fit to an idealized road-aligned rectangle per the owner's description of the real shape.

milestones.text: Listed as 'P11/11A' among the parcels RPD will manage (not among the 'when built' parcels) in OCII's Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation -- an upper bound on when this median was built, not its actual construction date

changes.text: The P11 median strip's shape file cited nothing. It now lists the OCII 2023 transition presentation, the OCII Dec 2019 Land Use Map, the OCII Nov 2024 CAC update and SF Rec & Park's Workshop 3 deck. The record said OCII's 2023 presentation lists 'P11/11A' as already managed by Rec & Park; the deck says Rec & Park 'will manage' them, so the wording now follows it, and the physical description is labelled as resting on this repository's own trace. The owner's identification of the strip as P11 is unchanged but flagged: OCII's 2024 update and Rec & Park's Workshop 3 timeline ('P11 opens - Mission Bay Commons (2015)') group P11 with the Commons, so the owner should settle what P11 covers. The Wikimedia aerial credit names only the Commons username Firstcultural, and the own-log source is labelled as such.

open_questions: No public source names this specific median strip or gives its own construction date; the Sept 2023 OCII document only establishes it existed and was already RPD-managed by that date (grouped with P11A), which is an upper bound, not a build date.

A separate, later OCII source (the Nov 2024 CAC deck, src-ocii-openspace-2024) instead groups the label 'P11' together with P12, P13, P15, P16 and P17 under the still-interim 'Mission Bay Commons' area near 3rd Street and Mission Bay Boulevard -- a different location from this record's median strip near Mission Bay Circle. This repo's own digitization_method log already describes correcting an earlier session's own wrong location guess for P11 (made from that same source note) after the property owner pointed to this median strip instead; the underlying conflict between the two OCII documents' own use of 'P11' is not resolved here, only flagged.
Owner/operator beyond 'part of RPD's Mission Bay open-space inventory' not confirmed by any source found.

Identity of P11 is unresolved and is the owner's call: SF Rec & Park's Workshop 3 deck (p.15 timeline, 2025-04-29) lists 'P11 opens - Mission Bay Commons (2015)', and OCII's Nov 2024 CAC update groups P11 with P12, P13, P15, P16 and P17 as 'Mission Bay Commons'. OCII's Dec 2019 Land Use Map and Nov 2024 p.2 map are reported to place a 'P11' label just east of Mission Bay Circle, where this strip is. Whether P11 is this 4.8 m median or a larger Commons segment has not been settled.
